newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end lower as share prices come off lows.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end lower as share prices come off lows.

text.p: Key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures ended lower on Monday after extending losses toward the close due to position-adjustment sales and as Tokyo share prices came off the day's lows, traders said.
"Concern about the downside risk of share prices had supported JGBs, and when stock prices came off the day's lows, this led to selling of JGBs," a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
The June ended at 126.48, down from Friday's close of 126.71.
Some traders said JGBs were heavy on top due to a series of recent corporate bond launches, but others downplayed the effect of the straight-bond launches.

"There is a limit to how much can be absorbed, despite strong investor strong demand for cash bonds...20-year JGBs were a bit heavy today due to an increased supply of 20-year cash bonds," a brokerage house trader said.
On Monday, both Chubu Electric Power and Tohoku Electric Power launched 50 billion yen 3.13 percent 20-year straight bonds.
Rather than taking a cautious stance toward corporate bonds, investors are hungry for bonds with coupon rates around three percent, a trader for a major brokerage house said.

"Investors want to see more bond issues with coupon rates above or near three percent, regardless of length of maturity. Rather than worrying about an excessive supply of bonds, they are eager to see more bonds launched," he said.
The supply and demand balance of the bond market is unlikely to slacken in the near-term, said Katsuzo Sakamoto, general manager at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd's bond & finance division.

Investor demand for corporate bonds has been strong recently, and other factors, including an expected drop in the issue amount of private-placement municipal bonds, is likely to keep the supply-and-demand balance of the bond market wound tight, Sakamoto said on Reuters Financial Television.

"According to our estimates, the issue amount of private-placement municipal bonds is likely to fall to about 3.8 trillion yen over March to May of this year, from approximately 4.9 trillion over the same period last year," he said. The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.175 percent as of 0649 GMT, up from Friday's close of 2.160 percent.
Traders said there was talk that investors seemed to be buying long-term and medium-term cash JGBs.
There was talk that life insurers were buying the 182nd JGB as well as medium-term JGBs, the first trader said.
There was also a rumour that public funds had bought the 182nd and 190th 10-year JGBs on Monday, the second trader said.

A speech on Monday by Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita was not a source of fresh trading incentives, traders said. Matsushita said the Japanese economy may slow down temporarily due to the recent increase in the sales tax but the recovery was likely to continue after this setback.
